title: Probe / Eval Weekly Synthesis — Aug 23 2027
content:
Purpose and framing:
This note captures the applied-ml probe/eval group’s work and open questions for the week of Aug 23–26, 2027. Focus areas: compact quant onboarding (edge CPU targets), KV-prefetch interactions with cached prefixes, and the eval harness changes needed to measure user-visible regressions across quant variants. The goal is a short synthesis for engineering partners and product owners — decisions, experiments, and next actions.

Attendees / context:
- Aisha Patel (owner, probe lead)
- Ravi Kapoor (quant infra)
- Zoe Kim (model onboarding / tokenization)
- Mateo Ruiz (perf infra / traces)
- Hannah Lee (evaluation / metrics)
- Notes pulled from async threads in #applied-ml and the sprint retro.

Key outcomes this week (top 3):
1) A minimal onboarding checklist for compact-quant variants that reduced manual steps by ~40% in our trial with the 3B architecture (step list below). Approved as a stopgap while the automation hooks land.
2) Identified a recurring mismatch between KV-prefetch assumptions and prefix cache hits that causes tail latency spikes under bursty traffic; reproducible with the new micro-benchmark harness.
3) Eval harness v2 merged to feature/structured-eval with instrumentation to attach per-prompt regression labels and automatic delta aggregation per rollout slice. First run produced an actionable regression signal on instruction-following tasks for q4_4bit.

Summary of experiments run:
- Compact quant accuracy sweep (3B)
  - Variants: q8_128, q4_256, q4_32-delta (our internal names).
  - Dataset: 2k synthetic instructions + 500 held-out human prompts (diverse instruction styles).
  - Metric: exact-match for structured outputs + normalized ROUGE-L for free-form answers.
  - Result: q4_32-delta shows a 1.9% decrease in ROUGE-L versus float32, but exact-match drops only on edge-case templates that use rare tokens and long single-token continuations. Qualitative inspection suggests tokenization mismatch more than quant noise.

- KV-prefetch microbenchmark
  - Setup: bursty sequence of shaped requests (prefix length distribution 5–120 tokens), with pre-warmed kv-cache for common prefixes and simulated prefetch window size 16.
  - Observation: when cache hit rate falls below ~70% and prefetch attempts overlap (concurrent small requests), latency p95 jumps by ~110ms compared to baseline. Root cause: prefetch worker queue thrashing and lock contention around kv-index updates.
  - Quick fix tested: reduce prefetch parallelism from 8 to 2 per runtime slot — p95 improved but throughput dropped for long-prefix workloads. Needs smarter backoff.

- Eval harness regression detection (canary run)
  - Run: rollout of q4_4bit on 3 dedicated instances for canary traffic (5% of overall).
  - Signal: per-slice delta on instruction-following score indicated a 3.4% relative degradation on a slice we label "multi-step reasoning with enumerated outputs".
  - Follow-up: tagged 120 prompts as a reproducer bucket and assigned to Zoe + Hannah for targeted triage.

Open technical questions and hypotheses:
- Tokenization vs. quant noise: the majority of exact-match failures on q4_32-delta map to long rare-token continuations (e.g., multilingual named entities). Hypothesis: quantized logits for those high-index tokens fall below softmax noise threshold, causing different top-1 picks. Proposed short test: recompute logits at higher internal precision at final softmax stage (hybrid final-cast) and measure delta.

- Prefetch backpressure policy: current naive parallel prefetch has no global view of slot occupancy. Hypothesis: implement a sliding-window admission control (based on recent cache hit ratio and request arrival rate) will stabilize p95 without sacrificing throughput. We sketched an admission algorithm (see action items).

- Eval slice sensitivity: the harness currently uses ROUGE-L + custom instruction-following heuristics. We need an additional automatic prompt-minimization step (binary search reducing prompt tokens while preserving regression) to shrink reproducers for faster debugging.

Decisions made this week:
- Merge eval-harness v2 to feature/structured-eval (Ravi approved). This will be the default harness for new quant onboarding runs.
- Defer automatic final-cast hybrid strategy to next sprint — we will first collect failing prompt reproducers using the new harness.
- Prioritize prefetch backpressure prototype over throughput-optimized prefetch until p95 stability target met for Dedicated customers (SLO goal: p95 < 120ms extra latency contribution).

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Aisha: Produce a 1-page automation spec for the compact-quant onboarding checklist (due 2027-08-30). Will include CLI steps, required artifact signatures, and smoke-check commands.
- Zoe: Triage 120 reproducer prompts for multi-step enumeration failures; produce 3 minimal reproducers and a hypothesis per repro (due 2027-08-28).
- Ravi: Implement sliding-window admission prototype in prefetch service, push a canary feature flag (due 2027-09-02).
- Mateo: Add detailed trace spans to prefetch code path to capture queue wait times and lock hold durations; correlate with microbenchmark (due 2027-08-27).
- Hannah: Extend eval-harness v2 with prompt-minimizer scaffolding and integrate as optional step for regression triage (due 2027-09-03).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Aggressive prefetch throttling could increase average latency for long-prefix loads and hurt embeddings-heavy customers. Mitigation: route long-prefix traffic through a separate path that keeps higher prefetch parallelism and uses per-customer config.
- Risk: False-positive regressions from new eval harness due to sampling variance. Mitigation: require regressions to persist on 3 independent runs and add bootstrap confidence intervals to per-slice deltas.

Notes from async threads (high-signal snippets):
- Ravi: "Prefetch worker contention isn't just CPU — the kv-index update holds a rw-lock which skyrockets when multiple prefetch tasks try to insert new entries simultaneously; we should consider lock-free append or batched inserts."
- Zoe: "For multilingual entities we saw tokenization fragmentation: a single entity splits into multiple rare subword tokens causing quant noise to amplify — short-term, force single-token mapping in tokenizer for these classes."
- Mateo: "The microbenchmark can reproduce the p95 spike by changing arrival jitter; will upload harness and script. Also discovered one misconfigured runtime-executor param that doubled queue length under test."

Documentation / artifacts updated this week:
- eval-harness v2 merged (see linked PR).
- onboarding checklist draft added to the onboarding/ directory (pending automation spec).
- microbenchmark harness v0.3 pushed to repo with new scenarios (burst-10, burst-50, steady-100).

Requests for other teams:
- Runtime team: Can you review the proposed admission algorithm (attached in PR comments) for any hidden scheduling constraints? We need an initial review by 2027-08-29.
- SDK / Tokenization: Could you add a short token debug flag to the tokenizer CLI that prints single-token mapping suggestions for reproducers? This will help triage rare-token failures.

Ideas for next sprint (brainstorm backlog):
- Hybrid final-cast: compute logits in q8 but final softmax in float16 for heavy-tail tokens.
- Per-customer prefetch profiles: automatic tuning based on observed prefix-length distribution.
- Automated prompt-minimizer that leverages eval-harness deltas to create minimal reproducers and suggested fixes (tokenizer tweaks, quant profile adjustments).

Appendix: compact-quant onboarding minimal checklist (short form)
- Produce model artifacts: float32 weights + metadata + tokenizer fingerprint.
- Run local qual sanity (10 prompts, smoke check).
- Run eval-harness v2 full sweep (2k instr + 500 holdout).
- KV-prefetch integration test with pre-warm script (10k requests at mixed prefix lengths).
- Performance baseline: p50/p95/p99 and memory footprint.
- Create reproducer bucket for any slice > 2.5% regression; attach to ticket and assign.
- Signoff: applied-ml lead + quant infra approval.

If anything needs to be added or if someone prefers a different cadence for these syntheses (longer, more data tables embedded), call it out in thread or ping me offline.

-- Aisha

Provenance: composed from standup notes, PR comments, microbenchmark logs, and the #applied-ml channel; intentionally lightweight so it can be copy-pasted into sprint retrospective and into the weekly exec summary.
